title: City Council District 5
statement: The quarterly outcome report on the Alternative Response Initiative tells the story I already knew from the streets: East Oakland's violent crime sits at 31 against a city average of 23.8 — we are still paying for decades of under-investment. But the dispatch-live protocol is changing how we answer. Sentiment here runs 0.48 against the city's 0.34 — folks feel the difference when a health worker shows up instead of a squad car. I'm filing my District 5 dispatch performance audit now, because the numbers only matter if we hold the city accountable to them. This isn't about a report — it's about whether East Oakland finally gets the response we've been demanding. The Masjid An-Nur pantry feeds our neighbors every week; our response system should feed their safety the same way. That's the standard.

payload.text: District 5 cohort placement intake numbers are on file: first cohort placed ahead of the initial schedule, with youth entering apprenticeship tracks across health and workforce sectors. The dispatch performance audit for INIT-002 in East Oakland confirms the alternative response protocol is live and active in our district — dispatched calls are routing to health responders consistent with the deployment authorized in C107. Both items are submitted and on the record for the quarterly review.
